name: Conduct NIST AI RMF
description: NIST AI Risk Management Framework enforcement rules across GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, and MANAGE functions

rules.description: Block attempts to disable or bypass AI governance controls (NIST AI RMF GOVERN 2.2)
rules.message: AI governance policy bypass blocked — NIST AI RMF GOVERN 2.2 requires organisational AI policies to remain active.
rules.recommendation: AI governance policies must remain active and enforced. Never disable policy checks programmatically.

rules.description: Block agents requesting system-wide permissions beyond their defined scope (NIST AI RMF GOVERN 1.2)
rules.message: Privilege escalation beyond agent scope blocked — NIST AI RMF GOVERN 1.2 requires least-privilege access for AI systems.
rules.recommendation: AI agents must operate under least-privilege. Define explicit, minimal permission scopes and never escalate to system-wide access.

rules.description: Block autonomous consequential AI decisions without human review gate (NIST AI RMF GOVERN 6.1)
rules.message: Autonomous consequential decision blocked — NIST AI RMF GOVERN 6.1 requires human oversight for high-stakes AI decisions.
rules.recommendation: Consequential AI decisions must include a human review gate. Implement an approval step before any irreversible automated action.

rules.description: Warn when AI deployed in high-risk domain without documented assessment (NIST AI RMF MAP 5.1)
rules.message: AI deployment in high-risk domain — NIST AI RMF MAP 5.1 requires documented risk assessment before deploying AI in consequential contexts.
rules.recommendation: Complete a risk assessment documenting the AI context, potential harms, affected populations, and mitigation controls before deploying in high-risk domains.

rules.description: Warn on passing unverified external data directly into AI model context (NIST AI RMF MAP 1.5)
rules.message: Unverified external data passed to AI model — NIST AI RMF MAP 1.5 requires validating data sources before use in AI systems.
rules.recommendation: Validate, sanitise, and document the provenance of all data before passing it to an AI model. Never pipe raw external input directly into model context.

rules.description: Block disabling monitoring or telemetry on AI systems (NIST AI RMF MEASURE 2.5)
rules.message: AI system monitoring disabled — NIST AI RMF MEASURE 2.5 requires continuous monitoring of AI system behaviour.
rules.recommendation: Monitoring and telemetry must remain active on AI systems. Adjust log levels rather than disabling tracing infrastructure.

rules.description: Warn on swallowed exceptions in AI pipeline code (NIST AI RMF MEASURE 2.2)
rules.message: Swallowed exception in AI pipeline — NIST AI RMF MEASURE 2.2 requires AI failures to be captured and logged for incident analysis.
rules.recommendation: Never swallow exceptions in AI processing pipelines. Log errors with context so failures can be analysed and trigger incident response.

rules.description: Warn on use of unapproved third-party AI providers without vendor assessment (NIST AI RMF MANAGE 4.1)
rules.message: Third-party AI provider detected — NIST AI RMF MANAGE 4.1 requires vendor risk assessment before using external AI services.
rules.recommendation: Document third-party AI providers in your vendor registry. Ensure DPA, security review, and liability terms are in place before production use.

rules.description: Warn on indefinite retention of AI conversation or inference data (NIST AI RMF MANAGE 2.4)
rules.message: Indefinite AI data retention detected — NIST AI RMF MANAGE 2.4 requires data retention limits aligned with stated AI purpose.
rules.recommendation: Define and enforce retention limits for AI inference data. Conversation and prompt logs should expire after the period necessary for the stated purpose.

rules.description: Warn when AI system deployed without owner/team tag for accountability (NIST AI RMF GOVERN 1.7)
rules.message: AI system deployment without accountability tag — NIST AI RMF GOVERN 1.7 requires clear ownership for every AI system in production.
rules.recommendation: Tag every AI deployment with owner, team, and responsible-contact metadata. Unowned AI systems cannot be managed or responded to in an incident.
